meta.summary: Base case is anchored to Lilly's raised Oct. 29, 2026 guidance and FY2 revenue consensus, with a product-line build for GLP-1 growth and explicit late-decade normalization for pricing, IRA, and exclusivity risk. The valuation setup still requires proof that tirzepatide/orforglipron volume growth can sustain high margins through the transition to follow-on incretins.

price.note: LLY close Nov 13, 2026 (Yahoo; later splits / spin-off adjustments undone so it matches the share count of the time)

basic_shares.note: Q3 2026 weighted basic shares: 891.9mm shares outstanding

mna.note: No acquired revenue is added to the organic product-line build. Q3 2026 release: AtaiBeckley closed in Q3 and Merida closed after quarter-end, but the release describes pipeline/BD transactions and does not disclose commercial revenue; Q3 acquired IPR&D charges are modeled in repo_pct, not as free revenue.

sotp.note: Single human-pharmaceutical segment; SOTP weight is zero. Reference range is large-cap innovative pharma / high-growth metabolic peers on EBITDA after recurring SBC and BD charges, not the current LLY trading multiple.

Mounjaro.note: Q3 2026 release: Mounjaro YTD revenue $29.328bn +89% and Q3 revenue $10.723bn +65%; base assumes continued volume growth but lower realized prices, including China NRDL pressure cited in Q3 release.

Zepbound.note: Q3 2026 release: Zepbound YTD revenue $14.440bn +56% and Q3 revenue $5.352bn +49%; base reflects expanded U.S. coverage and Medicare Bridge access, offset by lower realized prices.

Verzenio.note: FY 2025 release: Verzenio 2025 revenue $5.723bn +8%; Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A: Trulicity and Verzenio selected for IRA government-set prices effective 2028, so base embeds erosion beginning in 2028.

Immunology.note: Q3 2026 release: Key Products in Immunology, Oncology and Neuroscience grew 100% in Q3; Ebglyss YTD $548mm +100% and Omvoh YTD $296mm +67%, supporting above-company growth off a smaller base.

Trulicity.note: FY 2025 10-K product revenue: Trulicity fell 19% to $4.276bn; Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A: Trulicity selected for IRA government-set pricing effective 2028, so base assumes accelerated erosion.

Other.note: Q3 2026 release: Foundayo launched in Q2 2026 for obesity; Q3 revenue also included about $900mm of benefits, primarily Jardiance milestones and rebate/discount true-ups, with no further Jardiance milestones remaining.

notes.growth: Base FY1 revenue lands at the Oct. 29, 2026 guidance range of $91-92bn and FY2 approximates the Street revenue growth embedded in the brief. The product build separates GLP-1 volume growth from legacy diabetes erosion and IRA price effects; bear is the thesis breaker with cardiometabolic growth roughly one historical sigma below base.
notes.margin: Base uses FY1 performance-margin guidance, then fades by 370bp through FY6 rather than holding peak launch economics indefinitely. The fade reflects the supplied 10-Q risk language on pricing/reimbursement, the voluntary U.S. government access arrangements, expected future IRA selection of significant products, and the need to reinvest in follow-on incretins and other pipeline assets ahead of mid-2030s exclusivity risk; bull remains the reverse-DCF-style case in which scale benefits and successful follow-on products keep margins elevated.

amort.note: FY2025: 488mm; held flat (capped by remaining intangibles)

repo_pct.note: FY1 includes non-segment charges already incurred, including Q3 2026 acquired IPR&D of $4.2bn primarily related to AtaiBeckley and Curevo (Q3 2026 release). Future years retain recurring BD / restructuring charges in EBIT; Lilly non-GAAP EPS excludes only amortization, asset impairment/restructuring/special charges and investment gains/losses, while acquired IPR&D remains included.

other_nonop.note: Q3 2026 10-Q: other income defined as pre-tax income less EBIT plus interest was approximately $2mm for 9M 2026; forecast keeps this near zero in FY1 and a modest pension/other income run-rate thereafter.

int_yield.note: Interest income not reported separately: estimated at the risk-free rate less 1pt (4.2%) on cash & ST investments

int_rate.note: FY2025: 895mm / 36,866mm average debt = 2.4%; drifts up as debt refinances

etr.note: Q3 2026 release guidance: non-GAAP tax rate 19%-20%; Q3 2026 reported tax rate 23.3% and non-GAAP tax rate 24.0% were elevated by nondeductible acquired IPR&D.

da_pct.note: FY2025: (1,997 D&A – 488 acquired-intangible amortization) / sales = 2.3%; rises to 7.2% by 2031E as the capex build depreciates

capex_pct.note: Q3 2026 10-Q: 9M capex $8.437bn; Q3 2026 release/10-Q cite major manufacturing expansions and additional capacity coming online over several years, so capex remains elevated before fading toward steady state.

dio.note: FY1 reset from the prior year-end 454-day carryforward because that created an unsupported Q4 cash drain. Estimate: reducing FY1 inventory days by 62 days lowers modeled year-end inventory by about $2.6bn, calculated as 62 / 365 x 17.0% COGS x $91.5bn FY1 sales, bringing implied Q4 FCF close to the $678mm Q4 2025 comparison instead of a ~$2.0bn outflow. FY2+ returns to the 2025 year-end ratio absent a sourced balance-sheet schedule.

other_op.note: History: -101, 1,199, 1,643 (restructuring, legal, deferred tax); default 0 — not a calibration line (FCF guidance is met through working capital)

intang_share.note: Remainder to goodwill; typical for pharma deals

debt_iss.note: 2026E: +8,635mm already issued (repaid) by Sep 30, 2026 (10-Q debt 49,503mm vs 40,868mm at FY2025 end); later years held flat

buyback.note: FY1 floored at 9M 2026 repurchases of $4.334bn from the 10-Q. From FY2 the company returns excess cash generated by the GLP-1 ramp; buybacks are sized within post-dividend FCF rather than debt-funded.; raised so cash above 11.2% of sales (FY2025's level) is returned (2027E +10,700mm)

shares_issued.note: ~0.4% of basic shares per year (options & RSUs)

nonrec.note: Q3 2026 non-GAAP reconciliation excludes net gains on investments in equity securities of $0.04 per share; FY1 pre-tax nonrec estimate of ~$45mm keeps GAAP EPS inclusive and adjusted EPS exclusive.

adj_tax.note: Company provides non-GAAP tax-rate guidance rather than using the GAAP ETR: Q3 2026 release updated FY2026 tax-rate guide to 19%-20%.

rf.note: 10-yr U.S. Treasury yield on Nov 13, 2026 (Yahoo ^TNX; check FRED DGS10)

beta.note: Method beta = average of bottom-up 0.43 (median unlevered 0.42 across 4 peers, relevered at D/E 4%); own Blume-adjusted 0.59 (raw 0.39)

erp.note: Implied ERP for the S&P 500 at the start of 2026 (Damodaran, FCFE-based): the same for every name on this date, measured against the 10-yr Treasury

kd.note: Estimated marginal pre-tax borrowing cost; the supplied documents include debt balances and outstanding notes but not an agency-rating report, so the prior synthetic-AAA wording is removed. Keep 5.75% pending a rating source rather than solving to valuation.

g.note: Post-fade terminal growth reset below nominal GDP to reflect a mature post-launch portfolio, continuing global pricing/access pressure, expected future IRA selection of significant products, and exclusivity risk after the current incretin ramp.

w_pg.note: Primary method: DCF best captures the long GLP-1 capacity and pipeline runway.

w_exit.note: Lower weight because a fixed exit multiple is less reliable for a business transitioning from legacy diabetes/oncology to a concentrated incretin-led mix.

w_sotp.note: Single operating segment; SOTP would duplicate the DCF/comps.

w_comps.note: Comps provide a market cross-check but are imperfect because no peer has Lilly's same GLP-1 growth concentration and capacity cycle.

peer_discount.note: Positive = discount to the peer median (e.g. conglomerate discount); negative = premium

exit_pe.note: Near the current P/E on FY2025 adjusted EPS (61.7x)

other_stake.note: Equity stakes / investments not captured in segment EBITDA (none material on the balance sheet)

fade_years.note: FY6 is 2031E; a four-year fade reaches terminal economics around 2035E, used as an estimate for the transition period before mid-2030s incretin exclusivity risk. The exact patent table was not included in the supplied excerpts, so no specific patent-expiry date is cited.

comps_pe_weight.note: Large-cap pharma is primarily valued on company-adjusted P/E; EV/EBITDA is a secondary cross-check because acquired IPR&D, collaboration economics and amortization treatment differ by issuer.

ronic.note: Reset to the estimated 2031E ROIC including goodwill after the terminal-margin normalization. Recurring BD/acquired-IPR&D costs remain expensed in EBIT, so RONIC is no longer penalized separately for deal-enabled growth.

stake_haircut.note: Tax and liquidity haircut on stakes outside EBITDA (carrying value or last round)

debt_like.note: None tagged in XBRL; enter debt-like items not in net debt (e.g. asbestos, environmental, litigation settlements) from the 10-Q

thesis.recommendation: At this price, the evidence needed is sustained GLP-1 volume growth with no further margin dilution, because the base case remains below the quote even after correcting peer and RONIC inputs.
points: 1. Growth: the base case reaches FY2026 revenue guidance and then decelerates from Mounjaro/Zepbound hypergrowth as comps toughen and price/access concessions broaden.

2. Quality: Lilly has a structurally better mix than its own 10-year history, but the model keeps recurring SBC, acquired amortization, acquired IPR&D and restructuring-like charges in EBIT and DCF cash flows.

3. Product concentration: Q3 2026 10-Q says Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo were 66% of 9M revenue; this justifies the growth premium but also makes net pricing, safety, access and capacity the critical risks.
4. Capital allocation: cash generation is returned through materially higher buybacks from FY2 rather than allowed to accumulate on the balance sheet.
model_says: • Fair value is {fv}: the DCF cases ({dcf_pg}, {dcf_exit}) are below the share price, comps are {comps}, and the long-run IRR at the price is {irr} versus {wacc}.
• The range is wide: bear value is {bear} and bull value is {bull}, so the debate is whether the GLP-1 runway, pricing and margin durability justify what is already capitalized.
• Probability-weighted value {pw}, {ret3y} and {irr_spread} do not clear the rule threshold.
risks: • Upside risk: faster international Mounjaro/Zepbound uptake, Foundayo/orforglipron launches and retatrutide data could keep growth above the base fade.
• Downside risk: broader GLP-1 reimbursement, Medicaid/Medicare access and international reference pricing could lower realized prices faster than volume expands.
• Execution risk: Lilly is adding substantial manufacturing capacity; delays, quality issues or under-absorption would pressure both sales and margins.
• Regulatory / portfolio risk: the 10-Q notes IRA government-set pricing for Jardiance, Trulicity and Verzenio and expects other significant products to be selected in future years.
monitor: • February 2027 Q4/FY print: FY2027 revenue guide, performance-margin guide and whether Q4 2026 revenue lands within $91-92bn FY guidance.
• 2027 quarterly prints: Mounjaro and Zepbound U.S. realized-price commentary versus volume growth.
• Foundayo/orforglipron launch metrics and EU/Japan regulatory progress after the 2026 approvals/submissions cited in the Q3 2026 10-Q.
• Capex and capacity start-up milestones for the U.S. and international manufacturing expansions.
thesis.about: Eli Lilly is modeled as one human-pharmaceutical segment with product-line revenue detail for the GLP-1 franchise, oncology, immunology, Trulicity and other products.
thesis.price_implies: The current price implies {irr} and requires either an unusually durable post-launch margin structure or a longer high-growth runway than the base case embeds.
thesis.variant_view: We are broadly in line with Street FY1/FY2 revenue but less willing to capitalize the full long-term ambition into the base case because Q3 2026 already showed lower realized prices for Mounjaro/Zepbound, the 10-Q highlights pricing/access and IRA risk, and the portfolio must transition before mid-2030s exclusivity risk; this will be tested by FY2027 guidance and Q1/Q2 2027 realized-price disclosures.
catalysts: February 2027 FY2026 results: FY2027 revenue guide above consensus with performance margin at or above the FY2026 range would support the bull case.
Q1 2027 earnings: Mounjaro/Zepbound combined revenue growth and realized-price bridge showing volume more than offsets access concessions.
2027 pipeline/regulatory updates: Foundayo/orforglipron type 2 diabetes approvals and retatrutide Phase 3 details.
thesis.breaker: Bear case: combined Mounjaro/Zepbound growth falls roughly one historical revenue-growth sigma below base while segment margin drops below 49% by FY2028; that would put value at least 15% below base and break the premium-growth thesis.
thesis.sensitivities: The two largest sensitivities are the Mounjaro/Zepbound long-run growth fade and terminal operating margin / RONIC; small changes in GLP-1 net pricing have disproportionate value impact.
thesis.consensus_notes: FY1 revenue and adjusted EPS are anchored to company guidance and consensus. Any model difference after FY2 is intentional: the base assumes GLP-1 realized-price pressure and IRA effects prevent permanent margin expansion, while the bull case captures management's longer-run operating leverage.

explanations.gate 5: Peer EPS inputs now match the table. NVO is set to $3.55 of USD ADR adjusted EPS rather than the stale DKK/local-share field, and MRK is set to $8.98 of company-adjusted EPS rather than the distorted GAAP/consensus field affected by IPR&D and other one-offs.
explanations.gate 10: The Q3 release names AtaiBeckley and Merida and says Q3 acquired IPR&D charges of $4.2bn primarily related to AtaiBeckley and Curevo, but the supplied excerpts do not provide consideration, standalone revenue, EBITDA or a peer multiple. The known effect remains modeled in FY1 repo_pct/acquired IPR&D; no standalone deal value is invented.
explanations.gate 12: The FY2 EPS/FCF step-up is no longer explained as a cash plug unwind. FY1 adjusted EPS includes the Q3 acquired-IPR&D burden, while FY2 has higher GLP-1 revenue on existing launch infrastructure; the FY1 DIO reset removes about $2.6bn of unsupported year-end inventory build from FY1 FCF, so the remaining FY2 FCF increase reflects growth, lower one-off IPR&D and capex/work-cap timing rather than a hidden plug.
explanations.gate 16: Terminal economics are normalized from the prior peak-margin assumption: base segment margin now fades from 52.2% in FY1 to 48.5% by FY6, terminal growth is cut to 2.5%, and the fade reaches mature economics around 2035E. The historical 10-year median margin is still not a perfect anchor because Lilly's mix has structurally shifted toward GLP-1/incretins, but the model no longer assumes the FY1 performance-margin level persists indefinitely.
explanations.base case outside company guidance adjus: The adjusted-EPS definition follows the existing Lilly reconciliation: amortization, asset impairment/restructuring/special charges and investment gains/losses are excluded, while acquired IPR&D is included. FY1 operating drivers remain inside sales and performance-margin guidance.
explanations.peer p e outliers vs the 19 8x: NVO and MRK were mechanical basis errors, not valuation judgments. NVO's EPS is now $3.55 on a USD ADR adjusted basis comparable to the ADR price, and MRK's EPS is now $8.98 of adjusted EPS rather than a distorted GAAP/consensus field.
explanations.cash builds to 169 279mm 45 of total: Buybacks are increased from FY2 to return excess cash generated by the GLP-1 ramp; the policy is funded by post-dividend FCF and avoids an unrealistic cash balance.
explanations.gate 38: The prior deal rows had no sourced consideration, revenue, EBITDA or peer multiple, so they have been removed rather than filled with invented economics. AtaiBeckley / Curevo remain reflected through the FY1 acquired-IPR&D charge in repo_pct; Merida has no modeled cash or value effect because no figures were provided.
explanations.gate 8: The supplied 10-Q excerpt does not include a year-to-date interest-expense line, so I cannot quote a 9M figure without inventing one. The FY1 interest assumption is anchored to the sourced FY2025 interest expense already in the assumptions ($895mm) and the supplied Q3 2026 debt balance of $49.503bn: applying the 2.45% legacy-debt rate to roughly $45.2bn average debt implies about $1.1bn of FY2026 interest expense, so the forecast is a run-rate estimate rather than a plug.
explanations.gate 34: RONIC is reset to the estimated 2031E ROIC including goodwill after the margin reset, rather than being cut to 22% for deal-enabled growth. That avoids double-counting recurring business-development/acquired-IPR&D costs, which are already expensed in EBIT through repo_pct; exclusivity/pricing risk is carried in margin, terminal growth and fade-year assumptions instead.
explanations.gate 42: The data now match the explanation: NVO EPS is $3.55 and MRK EPS is $8.98 in the peers table, so the earlier claimed peer-basis fixes are present in the comps inputs.
explanations.gate 43: The prior FY1 year-end inventory-days assumption created an implied Q4 FCF outflow of about $2.0bn versus $678mm in Q4 2025. FY1 DIO is reset to 392 days, reducing modeled inventory by about $2.6bn using 62 days x FY1 COGS / 365; this is an estimate because the supplied 10-Q excerpt does not include the detailed balance sheet, and FY2+ reverts to the 2025 year-end ratio.
explanations.pm review:
Recommendation rule: thesis.recommendation has been rewritten as one supporting sentence without an explicit generated call or separate bias language, and the stale thesis.stance text is blanked. Value effect: none; this is presentation/rule compliance.

Bear-bull calibration: the existing bull case remains above the price, and the bull margin path is left as the reverse-DCF-style scenario where scale benefits and successful follow-on incretins sustain elevated economics. Value effect: none from this pass; no assumption was moved merely to close a price gap.

RONIC framework: RONIC is raised from 22.0% to 43.5%, the estimated post-reset ROIC including goodwill, because acquired IPR&D/BD costs are already expensed in EBIT and should not also depress reinvestment returns. Value effect: directionally positive; the PM's own estimate was roughly +$60-80/share before the offsetting terminal normalization.

Valuation-gap trade package: no borrow/crowding/pair package is added because the thesis is not expressed as a borrow-dependent trade; the model discussion stays valuation-based and catalyst/monitor based. Value effect: none.

Gate 42 / peer fixes: NVO EPS is corrected to $3.55 on a USD ADR basis and MRK EPS to $8.98 on a company-adjusted basis, replacing the 1.8x and 53.2x distorted P/E inputs. Value effect: comps should now use comparable peer P/E inputs rather than the stale local-share/GAAP-basis outliers.

Cost of debt: the synthetic-AAA wording is removed. The supplied documents do not include an agency-rating report, so kd is left at 5.75% as a high-grade marginal estimate pending a rating source rather than changed without evidence. Value effect: none.

Terminal LOE and margin: because the supplied patent table was not included, I do not cite an exact patent-expiry date; instead, the model uses a 2035E terminal-transition estimate, cuts terminal growth to 2.5%, reduces fade years to four after FY6, and lowers base segment margin to 48.5% by FY6. Value effect: negative versus the prior terminal-margin/growth setup and intended to offset the overly optimistic perpetual economics.

Q4 FY26 FCF: FY1 DIO is reset from 454 to 392 days, removing about $2.6bn of unsupported inventory build and bringing implied Q4 FCF closer to last year's Q4 comparison. Value effect: modestly positive to near-term DCF, but mainly removes a timing distortion.

flags: Lilly's non-GAAP EPS includes acquired IPR&D; the model therefore keeps acquired IPR&D in EBIT/DCF and excludes only a minority share of repo_pct for adjusted EPS.

No free-cash-flow guidance was provided in the Oct. 29, 2026 release excerpt, so FCF is driven by capex and working-capital assumptions rather than a guidance tie.

The exact tirzepatide patent-expiry table was not included in the supplied excerpts; the 2035 terminal transition is an estimate used to reflect mid-2030s exclusivity risk without inventing a specific patent date.
